business_problem: Wikimedia Deutschland needed to make Wikidata’s massive, multilingual knowledge graph usable for modern generative AI applications because the existing access pattern depended on specialized query languages and complex retrieval workflows that limited natural-language exploration.
solution_summary: Wikimedia Deutschland introduced a semantic retrieval architecture built on IBM DataStax Astra DB inside IBM watsonx.data so generative AI systems can search Wikidata with vector techniques instead of handcrafted queries. The design stores and retrieves embeddings across the large graph of entities and relationships that underpin Wikidata, allowing large language models to identify relevant facts and context quickly across languages and topics. By combining vector search with Wikidata’s existing structured graph, the platform gives developers and researchers a natural-language entry point into one of the world’s largest open knowledge repositories while preserving the precision that comes from the underlying linked data. The team is using this architecture as a base for expanding language coverage, scaling to larger datasets, and improving how AI systems discover, navigate, and interpret open knowledge, turning Wikidata into a more practical foundation for downstream generative AI tools rather than just a reference dataset for specialists.

solution_components.name: IBM DataStax Astra DB
solution_components.role: Provides the vector database foundation that lets LLMs retrieve relevant entities and relationships from Wikidata semantically.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.data
solution_components.role: Hosts the AI-ready data architecture that combines vector search with Wikidata’s structured knowledge.

data_flow: Natural-language prompts are translated into semantic retrieval against embeddings stored in Astra DB within watsonx.data, relevant Wikidata entities and relationships are surfaced from the knowledge graph, and that context is returned to downstream generative AI applications and researchers for multilingual exploration.
business_outcome: Wikimedia Deutschland created a faster, simpler way for AI systems and developers to explore open knowledge, making Wikidata more accessible for semantic search and future multilingual generative AI use cases.
architecture_clues: The design shifts access from specialized query languages to vector search and semantic retrieval.
The team plans to add more languages and larger datasets to the same architecture.
The solution combines vector search with the precision of Wikidata’s structured knowledge graph.
